obligation: Internal report of a suspected CJI incident
citation: N92-R02: CJISSECPOL v6.1 IR-6a (binding through the CJIS Security Addendum sec. 3.01; 28 CFR 20.33(a)(7)); POL-03 4.2
trigger: Any workforce member suspects an incident affecting the AC-02 tenant, the AC-02 interface, or systems that administer them
deadline: Immediately, and no more than 1 hour after discovery
notify: Company incident line or the IT Manager (incident commander)
applies_at_this_tier: Yes - AC-02 contract incorporates the Security Addendum; POL-03 applies the same 1-hour rule to all incidents

obligation: Company notice to the sheriff's office (AC-02) of a suspected CJI incident
citation: N92-R02: CJISSECPOL v6.1 IR-6b; AC-02 contract; POL-03 4.4
trigger: Suspected incident that may involve CJI or CHRI
deadline: IR-6b sets no separate deadline. AC-02 contract and POL-03 4.4: within 1 hour of discovery, without waiting for the company's investigation
notify: AC-02 local agency security officer, who routes the report to the CJIS Systems Officer (CSO), SIB Chief or Interface Agency Official, and FBI CJIS ISO
applies_at_this_tier: Yes

obligation: Sheriff's report of a security violation to the CSO and the FBI (agency duty the company supports)
citation: N92-R02: CJISSECPOL v6.1 Appendix H, Security Addendum sec. 4.01-4.03
trigger: Security violation involving a contractor with CJI access
deadline: Addendum sets no deadline; follows the state CSA's procedure
notify: AC-02 reports to the CSO and the Director, FBI, with the actions taken by AC-02 and the company. The FBI may suspend access and require CHRI to be deleted or returned
applies_at_this_tier: AC-02 duty. The company supplies its actions and evidence to AC-02 on request

obligation: Company notice to the revenue agency (AC-01) of a possible FTI disclosure
citation: N92-R01: Pub. 1075 Exhibit 7 I(3) and I(13) (AC-01 contract); Pub. 1075 sec. 1.8.2; POL-03 4.4
trigger: Possible improper inspection or disclosure of FTI, including a breach or incident in the AC-01 tenant, its backups, or its interface
deadline: Immediately. Company target: within 1 hour of discovery, so AC-01 has most of its 24-hour window
notify: AC-01 disclosure officer
applies_at_this_tier: Yes

obligation: TIGTA and IRS Office of Safeguards report of an FTI incident or data breach
trigger: Discovery of a possible improper inspection or disclosure of FTI, or a data breach. Do not wait for an internal investigation to confirm FTI was involved
deadline: Immediately, and no later than 24 hours after discovery. The Office of Safeguards data incident report goes at the same time as the TIGTA call; details follow as known
notify: TIGTA Field Division Special Agent-in-Charge (for network intrusions, TIGTA Electronic Crimes and Intelligence Division) and the IRS Office of Safeguards (encrypted email titled "data incident report", no FTI in it)
applies_at_this_tier: AC-01 files. Sec. 1.8.2 also places the duty on any person who discovers a possible improper disclosure, so the company confirms with AC-01 within the 24 hours that the report was made and reports directly if it cannot confirm

obligation: Taxpayer notice after unauthorized FTI access (agency duty)
trigger: Disciplinary or adverse action is proposed against the agency employee responsible for an unauthorized inspection or disclosure
deadline: Written notice to the taxpayer; the agency confirms completion to the Office of Safeguards and shares any draft media release before distribution
notify: Affected taxpayers; IRS Office of Safeguards
applies_at_this_tier: No for this runbook: an external attacker is not an agency employee. AC-01 decides. The media-release step still applies: AC-01 shares drafts with the Office of Safeguards

obligation: Florida state agency ransomware report (AC-01, AC-03)
trigger: Ransomware incident at a state agency, including one in a contractor-hosted system the agency uses
deadline: No later than 12 hours after discovery of the ransomware incident (48 hours for other severity level 3-5 incidents)
notify: Cybersecurity Operations Center and the Cybercrime Office of the Florida Department of Law Enforcement
applies_at_this_tier: Agency duty. The company must notify AC-01 and AC-03 fast enough, and supply the required content: summary of facts, date of the most recent backup, its location, whether it was affected, whether it was cloud-based, types of data, estimated fiscal impact, and ransom demand details

obligation: Florida county and municipality ransomware report (AC-04 to AC-11)
trigger: Ransomware incident affecting a county or municipality ("local government" in 282.3185(2))
deadline: No later than 12 hours after discovery of the ransomware incident (48 hours for other severity level 3-5 incidents)
notify: Cybersecurity Operations Center, the FDLE Cybercrime Office, and the sheriff with jurisdiction over the local government
applies_at_this_tier: Agency duty for the 8 municipal customers. The company supplies the same content as for state agencies. AC-02 is a sheriff's office; it decides with its county whether 282.3185 reaches it, and receives the company's notice within 1 hour either way

obligation: Local government after-action report
trigger: Remediation of a cybersecurity or ransomware incident at a county or municipality
deadline: Within 1 week after remediation
notify: Florida Digital Service
applies_at_this_tier: Agency duty for AC-04 to AC-11. The company provides the incident summary, resolution, and lessons learned in time

obligation: Prohibition on ransom payment by Florida agencies
trigger: Ransom demand to a state agency, county, or municipality
deadline: Applies at all times: these customers may not pay or otherwise comply with a ransom demand
notify: Not a notice. Shapes the ransom decision (POL-03 4.7)
applies_at_this_tier: Binds AC-01, AC-03, and AC-04 to AC-11. The company will not pay in a way any agency customer objects to

obligation: Third-party agent breach notice to each affected agency
trigger: Breach of security (unauthorized access of electronic personal information, 501.171(1)(a)) in a system the company maintains for an agency
deadline: As expeditiously as practicable, but no later than 10 days after determination of the breach or reason to believe the breach occurred
notify: Each affected agency (the covered entity). Include all information the agency needs for its own notices
applies_at_this_tier: Yes - applies directly to the company as a third-party agent (501.171(1)(h))

obligation: Agency notice to Florida individuals
trigger: Breach of personal information of Florida residents (for example SSNs in AC-01 and AC-03 records, driver license numbers in municipal files)
deadline: No later than 30 days after determination of the breach or reason to believe it occurred; law enforcement may delay in writing (501.171(4)(b))
notify: Each affected Florida resident, by mail or email
applies_at_this_tier: Agency duty (governmental entities are covered entities for notice). The company may send notices on an agency's behalf if the agency asks (501.171(6)(b))

obligation: Agency notice to the Florida Department of Legal Affairs
trigger: Breach affecting 500 or more individuals in Florida
deadline: No later than 30 days after determination of the breach or reason to believe it occurred (15 more days for notice to individuals if good cause is given in writing within 30 days)
notify: Florida Department of Legal Affairs
applies_at_this_tier: Agency duty; likely for any tenant whose database was taken. The company supplies counts of Florida residents per tenant

obligation: Agency notice to consumer reporting agencies
trigger: Notice required to more than 1,000 individuals at one time
deadline: Without unreasonable delay
notify: All nationwide consumer reporting agencies
applies_at_this_tier: Agency duty if more than 1,000 are notified

obligation: Other states' breach laws
trigger: Affected individuals who live outside Florida (for example taxpayers who moved away)
deadline: Varies by state
notify: Residents and regulators under each state's law
applies_at_this_tier: Agency duty in each state where affected individuals reside; the company supplies residence data

obligation: SNAP, TANF, and Medicaid applicant data (AC-03)
trigger: Unauthorized access to AC-03 applicant or household data
deadline: The cited rules limit use and disclosure but set no incident notice deadline for the contractor. The company's clocks come from the AC-03 contract (POL-03 4.4) and Fla. Stat. 501.171(6)
notify: AC-03 information security manager
applies_at_this_tier: Yes - through the AC-03 contract. AC-03 decides any reporting to its federal program agencies

obligation: Supply chain incident coordination
citation: SP 800-53 IR-6(3) (Moderate baseline); CJISSECPOL v6.1 IR-6(3)
trigger: Incident involving a cloud or SaaS service in the platform
deadline: No deadline set; as soon as practicable
notify: Cloud provider security incident channel; identity provider vendor if sessions or tokens were abused
applies_at_this_tier: Yes - contract (SP 800-53 Moderate)

obligation: OFAC sanctions check before any ransom payment
citation: OFAC Updated Advisory on Potential Sanctions Risks for Facilitating Ransomware Payments (Sept. 21, 2021); 31 CFR ch. V
trigger: Any ransom payment is considered
deadline: Before any payment. Full and timely reporting to law enforcement or CISA is a mitigating factor
notify: OFAC (license if a sanctioned party is involved); FBI or CISA
applies_at_this_tier: Yes - all U.S. persons. Strict liability for payments to sanctioned parties

obligation: Law enforcement and CISA report (voluntary)
citation: OFAC advisory (Sept. 21, 2021) mitigating factor; company practice
trigger: Ransomware or data theft confirmed
deadline: Company target: within 48 hours of declaration
notify: FBI field office or IC3; CISA
applies_at_this_tier: Voluntary. Coordinate with the agencies, which report to FDLE under Florida law

obligation: Cyber insurance claim notice
trigger: Suspected security incident
deadline: Per policy; call the breach hotline before hiring any response vendor
notify: Carrier breach hotline
applies_at_this_tier: Yes - contractual, not legal

obligation: HIPAA breach notification
trigger: Breach of unsecured PHI
deadline: Not applicable
notify: Not applicable
applies_at_this_tier: No - no customer has designated the company a business associate; AC-03 placed its eligibility functions outside its health care component (45 CFR 164.105)

obligation: CIRCIA incident and ransom payment reports
citation: N92-R07: 6 U.S.C. 681-681g; proposed 6 CFR Part 226 (89 FR 23644)
trigger: Covered cyber incident or ransom payment
deadline: Proposed: 72 hours (incident); 24 hours after ransom payment
notify: CISA
applies_at_this_tier: NOT YET REQUIRED: no final rule in the Federal Register as of 2026-09-26. Recheck when a final rule is published

obligation: Covered telecommunications report
trigger: Covered equipment or Kaspersky covered article identified under a federal contract
deadline: Within 1 business day of identification
notify: Contracting officer
applies_at_this_tier: No - the company holds no federal contracts or subcontracts
